title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a terminological digression inside the 1986 'ateliers' notes. It continues the previous page, which proposed shifting the main emphasis, and the name 'atelier', from the figures F to the base set M.

Setup in modern terms:
- M is a set of 'strates' carrying an incidence/specialisation relation, essentially a poset.
- Each strate X determines X̃, the set of its sub-strates (the strates incident to X). X̃ is the principal down-set of X, i.e. its closure in the Alexandrov topology of the poset, like the set of faces of a cell or simplex.
- Grothendieck decides to call the elements X ∈ M 'strates' and X̃ the 'multistrate' associated to X.

For a figure F:
- The 'strates of F' are the elements of F̃, the strates of M incident to F.
- The 'multistrates of F' are the X̃ for X ∈ F̃.
- The set of these multistrates could be written F̃̃ (double tilde).

The concrete model is Figil(L) = M, the atelier of figures described as multistrate sets on a ground set L. There an object of M is itself a set of parts of L, an element of P(P(L)), much as a simplex is identified with its set of faces. Even so, he insists it is still called a 'strate' and not a 'multistrate'.

The next page draws the type-theoretic consequences:
- a strate lies in P(P(L));
- a multistrate X̃ lies in P(P(P(L)));
- since figures are now just parts of M, F̃ = F and the 'déploiements' of a figure become superfluous;
- unless one later restores autonomy to F via a mixed structure (M, F) with an incidence relation Δ.

The purpose is to fix vocabulary for a combinatorial or stratified model of 'tame' geometric figures: strata, their closures, and figures as unions of closed strata.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page is purely terminological. There is a slight type ambiguity: a 'strate' of Figil(L) is already a set of parts of L, which Grothendieck explicitly acknowledges and resolves on this and the next page.

ideas.what: A strate X determines X̃, the set of its sub-strates (incident strates), called the multistrate of X.
ideas.modern_name: Principal down-set / closure of a point in a poset with the Alexandrov topology; face set of a cell in a face poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937); standard in combinatorial topology (face posets of regular CW complexes)
ideas.where_published: Stratification ideas appear in Esquisse d'un programme (§5–6, tame topology, 'dévissage' of stratified structures); this specific terminology is not known to be published.

ideas.what: Figures F as down-closed sets of strates, with F̃ the set of strates of F and F̃̃ the set of their multistrates.
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplexes / closed (down-closed) subsets of a stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorics of posets and CW complexes

ideas.what: Figil(L): the atelier of figures given as set systems on a ground set L, with strates as elements of P(P(L)).
ideas.modern_name: Abstract simplicial complexes / set systems on a vertex set L

deep.surprise_reason: Pure terminology: renaming strates and multistrates and noting the set-theoretic type of objects in Figil(L). The underlying mathematics (posets of strata, down-sets, set systems) is standard. Only the unpublished 'atelier' framework itself is of historical interest, and this page adds no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is likely 'Il vaut la peine de préciser [?] la terminologie possible strates – multistrates' rather than 'Il vaut le [?] périphraser'; this is uncertain.

'On pourrait désigner l'une [?] de ces multistrates' should probably read 'On pourrait désigner l'ensemble de ces multistrates par F̃̃'. The handwriting suggests 'l'ens.', and the set reading fits the double tilde.

'des figures définies [-comme-] comme ensembles [?] multistrates [?] sur un ensemble L' probably reads 'des figures définies comme ensembles multistrates sur un ensemble L' (or 'ensembles multistratés').
The '38' at bottom left is the archive page number; '35' at top is Grothendieck's own numbering.
